title: Queen Anne to the Earl of Peterborough, instructions, St James's, 22 Feb 1711/12 (BL Add MS 4107 ff. 184-185; DECODE R4878)

documents.shelfmark: British Library, Add MS 4107, ff. 184r-185r; DECODE R4878

plaintext.source: G. Parke (ed.), Letters and Correspondence of Henry St. John, Lord Visc. Bolingbroke (1798), vol. 1 pp. 310-311: the whole instructions in clear.

transcription.source: DECODE R4878 images (300 dpi); transcription.txt, code runs in alignment.tsv.
transcription.notes: Counts from align.py over transcription.txt (the --measure tool counts clear words as well). Two groups lost in the gutter of f. 184v (52?, 33?).

system.summary: A numerical English code of groups 76-2269 with many nulls and some homophones, used for the sensitive phrases inside clear instructions.
system.sibling_key: none found: 155 transcribed British key records on DECODE tested against four anchors, no match
system.notes: 414 groups for 232 printed words; the code table was not rebuilt beyond about 20 anchor values. Homophones: Prince = 1076 and 2211; Rome = 1369 and 519.488. Not alphabetical: 466 he < 609 his < 894 him < 981 your.

prior_solution.where: Parke 1798, vol. 1 pp. 310-311 (clear text from the office draft)

conditions.human_role: Posed the target (catalogue item 86) and supplied DECODE access; no reading or source was supplied.

solution.what: Web search for a printed text of Peterborough's instructions of Feb 1712.
Downloaded the three DECODE R4878 images; no interlinear or marginal decipherment.
Transcribed the clear text and 61 code runs (414 groups).
From clear context: 894 = him, 466 = he, 894.1098 = himself, 981 = your; the order rules out a one-part code.
Tested 155 transcribed British DECODE keys (SP 106 boxes 6-8, BL/TNA keys 1690-1730, Add MS 61575) against the anchors.
Grepped the archive.org text of Parke's Bolingbroke correspondence (1798) for Peterborow: the instructions are printed in full, vol. 1 pp. 310-311.
Aligned all 61 runs with the print (alignment.tsv); recurring groups hold one meaning at every place (534 to x8, 678 the, 839 you, 894 him, 609 his, 1373 religion, 1219.563 Protestant).

outcome.method_basis: The clear text of the instructions is printed in full from the office draft in Parke's Bolingbroke correspondence (1798, vol. 1 pp. 310-311), found during the attempt after 155 DECODE keys failed; all 61 code runs were aligned to it, and only about 20 anchor values of the code were fixed.
outcome.notes: Every code run is matched to the printed clear text; two runs (91, 261) have no printed word. The code table itself is not rebuilt.
